title: The interpreter epoch: knowing when nothing has changed
summary: Architecture: Tom Dyer ('trigger on change': pass cached objects while nothing changed). ooRexx collections have no change notification, but while compiled code runs it holds the interpreter lock, so nothing changes until compiled code calls the interpreter. Every such call goes through the thread context's function table. include/rx_api_epoch.hpp replaces that table (from rxobj::Scope, at each native entry) with a copy whose functions bump a counter, the epoch, before and after calling the interpreter's own. RX_API_PURE lists the functions that cannot run Rexx code or change a collection; all others are in RX_API_BUMPS. Static asserts tie both lists to the ooRexx header (THREAD_INTERFACE_VERSION 103 and the struct size). A cache keyed by the epoch is valid while the epoch has not moved. First user: environment symbols (.NAME), see rx2cpp.environment-symbols.
invariants: A function not proven pure bumps the epoch.
DirectoryAt bumps: a Directory get can run an entry's SETMETHOD method or the Directory's UNKNOWN method. StringTableAt is pure (a StringTable has neither).
Entering and leaving compiled code bump; so do the method context's ForwardMessage and SetGuardOn/Off (rxobj::viaInterpreter).
If the ooRexx thread interface changes, the static asserts fail the build: update the two lists, do not silence the assert.

provenance.claim: Epoch design, PURE/BUMPS lists and static asserts.
